‘Delhi's air will be very bad after Diwali’: SC judge on request to defer a hearing
The issue of pollution in Delhi is being monitored by the Supreme Court in a suo motu proceeding arising from a petition filed by advocate MC Mehta.
Delhi’s air will be much worse after Diwali, commented Supreme Court judge Vikram Nath on Wednesday while entertaining a request to accommodate hearing of a matter for November 17.
The light-hearted comment by a bench headed by justice Vikram Nath exposed a sad reality of Capital’s deteriorating air quality. The issue of whether firecrackers will be allowed on Diwali this year is to be heard and decided by another bench of the Supreme Court on Thursday.
Also Read | Supreme Court: Firecracker ban needs a ‘pragmatic, practical’ approach
SC to hear plea on Diwali firecrackers on Thursday
Justice Nath said, “Post Diwali, the air in Delhi will be very bad.” He was responding to a request made by senior advocate Indira Jaising who appeared in a matter with a request to adjourn it to November 17.
The judge was willing to grant a date for the matter on November 3 as justice Nath, who is presently the senior most puisne judge in the Supreme Court, continued the light banter, “You come before Diwali, the environment would be cleaner. After Diwali, it will be worse.”
But the senior counsel remarked that before Diwali too, it will be no better. “Diwali is an extremely polluted time in Delhi. Please have the matter on November 17.” Continuing the light-hearted conversation with the bench, Jaising remarked, “Your lordships already have to suffer the bad air.”
As Jaising was appearing virtually before the court through the videoconferencing facility, justice Nath quipped, “You have the privilege of sitting at home and saving yourselves from the pollution. But we can’t sit at home.”
The issue of pollution in Delhi is being monitored by the Supreme Court in a suo motu proceeding arising from a petition filed by advocate MC Mehta. Along with this, in 2015, a petition was filed by three toddlers seeking a complete ban on firecrackers owing to the detrimental effect on children, aged and sick persons who face breathing and other health related complications.
Incidentally, both these matters are listed before a bench headed by justice MM Sundresh on Thursday. Under orders passed in the MC Mehta petition, there is a ban on bursting, sale and distribution of firecrackers in Delhi, extending further to the national capital region. Last year, a window was provided by the court for sale and bursting of crackers during Diwali in order to strike a balance between the right to health of citizens and the celebrations surrounding the right to observe festivals and religious beliefs.
This year too, the fireworks retailers have requested the court for a similar arrangement demanding that under monitoring of the court, specified dates could be allotted for sale of crackers and its bursting be regulated during specified times. This issue will be decided on Thursday.
Also Read | Supreme Court rules out blanket cracker ban ahead of Diwali: 'It will hurt sentiments'
SC calls for ‘practical and pragmatic’ approach
Early this month, the court indicated that banning firecrackers needs a “practical and pragmatic” approach. It emphasised that religious sentiments cannot be hurt and at the same time, the health of citizens must be taken into consideration by promoting the use of green crackers that are less harmful to public health.
While striking this middle path, the Centre has submitted formulations of improved crackers having less emission by involving experts including CSIR-NEERI, PESO and CPCB. The experts have presented formulations for next generation joined crackers, which are less polluting than conventional joined crackers (lari). They are presently undertaking studies on the reduced use of barium in firecrackers, for which open ground testing is being conducted across multiple places in the country.

Few people understand the current deepfake epidemic better than Jess Asato. The British Labour MP has spent years campaigning against the use of technology to abuse women and girls. Then, after calling out Elon Musk during the notorious Grok Deepfake Scandal of 2025, Asato found herself caught in the very crisis she had been trying to prevent.
Disturbing and degrading deepfake images of the MP circulated widely. One appeared to depict a sexual assault. When Asato reported them to X, the platform repeatedly dismissed her complaints. So she decided to take the fight somewhere else: the courts. She is now pursuing legal action against Musk’s xAI, arguing that it unlawfully used her image without her consent. The case could help establish a precedent for holding AI companies accountable when their products cause harm.
For Asato, this is personal, but it is hardly new territory. Before entering Parliament, she spent years working with charities supporting survivors of domestic abuse and vulnerable children. That experience has shaped her political career, informing her push for stronger protections for women and children online. Now, she is confronting more troubling questions: What happens when the technology enabling abuse becomes ubiquitous, the platforms hosting it refuse to intervene, and the people targeted are left to fight back on their own?
At stake for Asato is more than the misuse of a single image. It is whether consent still means anything when AI can manufacture almost anything, and whether the companies building these tools can be made to answer for what they do. Asato is betting that the law can catch up with the technology. And she is prepared to take on Musk to find out. (xAI did not immediately respond to WIRED’s request for comment.)
Also, before you read on, be aware that this interview includes references to sexual assault and child sex abuse.
This interview has been edited for length and clarity.
ROSIE SWASH: Jess, I just want to have a couple of warm-up questions before we get into it. Tell us a bit about your background, how did you end up becoming MP for Lowestoft?
JESS ASATO: Sure. So, I grew up in East Anglia in Norfolk and Suffolk, and in a not very political family. I got the politics bug in 1997 when Tony Blair was talking about education, education, education. Having experienced it, I felt that we could be doing a lot better in our education system. So I joined the Labour Party and got involved with my local groups.
Before Parliament, I worked for the largest children's charity in the UK for three years on their policy and public affairs, trying to change legislation on behalf of the most vulnerable children in the country. Six years prior to that I worked for a domestic abuse charity called SafeLives where we did huge amounts of work to try and improve the situation for survivors of domestic abuse, particularly through the Domestic Abuse Act.
Those twin issues of women and children have become my focus in Parliament, and I’ve been very clear that my reason for being here, my mission really, is to be a voice for women and children.
Well, that’s a good entry point for us to start talking about this year. So in early 2026, there was widespread reporting on Grok, xAI’s chatbot, being used to create sexualized images of children and women, and those images being circulated on X. How aware were you at this point of the phenomenon of deepfakes being used in this way?
Very aware, and actually had been working with survivors who had experienced deepfakes for quite a number of years. Ever since the advent of AI this has been happening to women, and there’s also been developing risks of children both being put into child sexual abuse material and also children using nudification tools on other children, thereby criminalizing themselves because these tools are so easy to access and often free.
So I was already very alive to the huge harms being created by AI deepfakes of both women and children before Grok ever happened. It was a known harm, which is why many of the tools from other companies had already taken steps to stop them from being used to create this kind of content.
There are a number of tools where, if you type in “nudify,” or “take the clothes off this person,” the tool will refuse to do that. So into that environment came Grok.
Was there a particularly egregious example or incident prior to Grok when you became aware of deepfakes that really stuck with you?
There is a brilliant campaigner who goes by the name of Jodie. I think it was probably listening to the experiences of Jodie, who was deepfaked, and it was such an affront to her that somebody would do this, and then she found out it was actually a friend. Such a betrayal of trust.
These things destroy not just the individual involved, but often families and everyone around them too.
For people who don’t know, who exactly was Jodie? Is this a constituent of yours or someone who came forward to you specifically?
No, no, no. She's a very well-known campaigner on this issue. That’s not her real name.
I know it sounds obvious, but what exactly is nudification?
It is where you ask an AI tool to take the image or video of a real person and use generative AI to make that person either nude, partially nude, or engaging in pornographic acts. This is something that, because of the photorealistic nature of AI images, it has become increasingly hard to see what is a fake image.
It can often look incredibly, incredibly real.
So what was it particularly about the Grok scandal earlier this year that made you want to raise this in the House of Commons?
It was the fact that we already knew that you could stop this from happening by designing the AI tool to reject the ability to do this.
This was completely avoidable. That’s why I spoke out, but also because I’d just spent a year and a half campaigning to get a ban on nudification apps, and here was an all-purpose AI tool becoming a nudification app.
It just felt to me as though we were making strides in the UK, and then the world’s richest man and his product decided to turn the clock back.
So what exactly did you stand up and say?
What I did was I talked about the need for the government to accelerate its ban on nudification apps, which it did. So the then secretary of state for science, innovation and technology, Liz Kendall, said that she was going to bring that ban into law through the Crime and Policing Act, which she did.
But I also said that it was very important that we went further than that, because, of course, Grok itself is not a sole-purpose nudification tool. It has a general use, and therefore we needed to bring all AI chatbots under the auspices of the Online Safety Act. That is also what eventually happened in the Crime and Policing Act, and we’re now waiting until that legislation comes into effect. There’s got to be a consultation, I understand, before it does.
So technically another Grok could happen in this period, but in the future there would be much stronger measures that we could take against tools like Grok creating nudification content.
So that’s a really positive outcome of your interjection in Parliament, but what else happened as a result of you standing up?
Well, one of the things that happened was that I posted on social media saying that Elon Musk should stop Grok from being able to do this.
And then, of course, I became a victim of the same trend. So Grok put this woman in a bikini. And most of the images were sort of pornified, I would say. They weren’t nude images, but they were me with inflated boobs in a bikini.
Then people tried to make it funny, I guess, by putting a swastika on me or hammer and sickles. Or making me pregnant with quintuplets and putting me in a kitchen. Because of course that’s the only use for women—birthing and making dinner. But the really disturbing one was a video of me being surrounded by a group of men, chloroformed over my mouth, and then I fall backwards onto a chair. Then my skirts are lifted up. So no nudity, but clearly the next frame is meant to be a sexual assault. So it was really distressing and disturbing.
That was the point at which a friend said, “You probably need to reach out to a lawyer.” Because each of these things we reported to X, and none of them contravened their terms and conditions. We just kept getting those sort of repeat emails coming back. “We’ve looked into this, and there’s nothing to see here.” So I did engage a lawyer, who sent a letter to X to ask for these to be removed, and they were.
But it was at that point that he said, “I think you might actually have a case. We think that xAI have broken the law.”
It’s impressive how you handled it, but it must have been really awful.
It was; it was awful. This is done to demean, to degrade, and to push women out of online spaces. From my perspective, I tend to use bad or difficult things that happen as a way of thinking about how we change this for the future.
My old boss was an amazing woman called Tessa Jowell. She used to say to me, “How do we change this negative energy into something positive?” “How do we work our way out of this into a place where we actually feel that we’ve learnt from it?”
So I guess she instilled in me that sense that when something bad happens you’ve got a choice. You can wallow in it, you can try and forget about it, or you can use it as a catalyst for change.
So I was quite trepidatious about the idea of taking on a legal action. Not least because of the person who is at the top of xAI, now SpaceXAI. [Eds. note: The company recently rebranded itself as SpaceXSI.] He’s the world’s richest man. But also because I didn’t want myself to necessarily be the story. Many, many women had things that were created of them through both Grok and other nudification tools that are much, much worse.
Having said that, I knew that if there was the opportunity to say that actually they’d broken the law, there was an important point of principle on behalf of all of the women and the children whose images were manipulated and misused by Grok, who would never, ever be able to bring a legal case. So I decided that I wanted to do this, because I wanted to be able to show that no one is bigger than the law.
Doesn’t matter how rich you are or how powerful you are or how big a reach you have in terms of your social media presence or who your friends might be at the top of various governments. If you break the law in our country, you need to feel the force of that. As an ex-lawyer and now as a legislator, it is important that we uphold our law where it has been broken.
So it’s also about giving control back, I think, to us as individuals, but also as a society. So many of these digital changes have been done without our consent or say, and I think there’s a feeling that there’s a sort of runaway train that we’re all on, whether we want to be or not, because we all need to use online spaces for our work, for connection.
And so my view is that we should be expecting companies to respect our law or at least make new laws to bring them more into line with what society really needs.
You said that you gave it some thought. In that moment of trying to decide how to respond, what are you weighing up? Who are you talking to? Are you going back and talking to your team or your family to work out how you should respond, knowing that it may invite further speculation and further attention?
My family mostly, my husband in particular. It’s one thing being a politician and arguing your case to change the law on behalf of women and children; it’s another having your own legal case.
So I was worried about the impact that that might have on my family, my children. I also know that this can bring danger to politicians. So I worried about the fact that I am obviously engaging and making the defendant somebody who has got this very wide reach on social media. However, I don’t like bullies. I very strongly believe that it’s important to fight on the field that you’ve got, and this was an opportunity I felt to make a difference.
So I weighed that up and thought that it was worth having that kind of attention and potential danger, because there is a bigger issue here that we need to get right.
When you say you don’t like bullies, are you talking about, let’s face it, men who used Grok in this way in the first place, or are you talking about Elon Musk?
I’m talking about the men who use this as a form of trying to push women out of the online space. Actually it was quite clear in quite a lot of the comments that they were saying, “Well, if you don’t like this, then get off the platform.”
Either that or, “If this is too hot for you, get out the kitchen,” which I always find quite funny because they put me in a kitchen. I think it’s really interesting when you look at X in terms of its demographics in the UK, it’s highly weighted toward men. I think some of that’s down to the fact that there is just so much misogyny and abuse on it. So I’m assuming, and correct me if I’m wrong, that the other side of the response to going public is that other women have come forward to you.
Absolutely. Actually, one of the heartening things has been people coming forward and saying, “Thank you, because this has now given me the license to actually accept that what happened to me wasn’t my fault. It’s not my shame.” So, in a way, what I’m hoping is that this has helped some victims to process what has happened to them and understand that this was not right.
I’ve also had emails from parents where they’ve said that this has happened to their daughter. It’s been done by boys at school. I’ve had teachers saying that boys have made pornographic AI imagery of them. And it’s something where we’ve just sort of let it happen and wash over us and accept that somehow this is now a part of the society we live in.
So yes quite a number of people have come forward. Obviously not all of their experiences have been through Grok, and I think one of the things is that often, when you see these films or images, you don’t know what platform they’ve been created on. I mean, the only reason why I knew it was Grok was because it was integrated with X, and you could see the commands that had been given by the users.
But much of the time, when this content is created, most victims don’t know by whom or on what platform. And so there’s really very little they can do about it. And I think it’s that sort of sense of helplessness that you have been violated, and that is the word that comes up so frequently from victims of this particular issue.
It’s not just that it’s nudified. Of course, much of my content wasn’t. It’s the lack of consent. And lots of people say, “Oh, but it’s fake. It’s just a laugh.” But what people don’t understand is that it is hyperrealistic, and it’s your face.
It’s a piece of your soul. It’s not just pixels on the internet. It is a person. And because obviously I’ve worked for a long time in violence against women and girls and spoken to many victims of sexual assault and to children who’ve been victims of child sexual abuse, it is the lack of consent that is so disturbing.
It can leave people with PTSD and quite deep trauma. And there have been a number of people I’ve met who have said that the world seems less safe to them because this has happened to them.
I think you’ve already touched on it, but what is the biggest myth around deepfakes that you would wish to dispel?
That it comes without any harm.
That it’s just a laugh.
There is clear harm, even when it’s not done to demean or degrade. So even if it’s done sometimes by friends, the fact is that you haven’t consented to that. There is something about the human psyche which is that when you see yourself so realistically created in a different situation or scenario, something that’s not something you would have done, I think it’s quite discombobulating.
I think your brain can’t quite process it because your brain knows it’s not true, but it looks very true. And I think psychologically we still don’t really understand how this content is going to change the way we think about our world, how we know what is true and what isn’t true.
Right.
Now, of course, you can do fantastic things with generative AI. All I’m calling for is that we respect people’s consent, and that’s why one of the things I’ve been working on since this happened is to look at whether we could create a system of consent to be manipulated by AI.
Could we create a greater right over our likeness online so that there’s a new social norm, which is that no, you can’t copy and paste that picture into an AI chatbot and do whatever you want with it. That’s not yours. It’s not your data. It’s their data, and you’re breaching the law if you do that.
I think if we were to do that, we could have a wide range of applications. It wouldn’t just be in this space of the sexualization of women and children. But also with political disinformation. We are so close to a moment where somebody produces a hyperrealistic video of a politician saying something that they didn’t, and then that leads to real-world harm. And so we’ve got to find a new social norm that says unless for public figures it’s parody or satire—and absolutely you’ve got to protect that—but in all other instances your picture, your voice, and your moving image is your personal data, and it’s not for anyone else to use.
So that’s interesting because you’re touching on new social norms and the possibility of new laws to keep up with this technology. But your lawsuit is specifically under a data law. Talk to me about that versus a law around consensual imagery or deepfakes specifically.
So, my case is brought under existing law, the GDPR, the data protection law, and it contends that Grok misused my data without my consent. It didn’t have consent to process my data, the data being my face and my likeness. But also under privacy laws that I had a reasonable expectation of privacy and that particularly the video of me being prepared for sexual assault reaches a criminal threshold and that nobody should be expected to be on the receiving end of.
Let’s remember, this is actually a product that has been designed by software engineers and developers, and that actually products should not lead to an invasion of privacy and the harm that I then experienced as a result of that, including distress and a sense that I was being harassed by this particular creation of this particular video.
So, it rests on good solid legal grounds, and we await the defense from SpaceX AI.
I don’t know how much you can say, legally, but what part of the process are you in? What happens next? What’s the timeline for a resolution to this case?
So like with a lot of legal cases, it’s very, very hard to pin down a timeline. But my understanding is that we should be receiving the response and the defense from SpaceXAI in the near future. But we don’t have a deadline or a particular time that I can put on it.
After that, my understanding is that the case will then be looked at, and if there is a case to answer, then it will go to a court hearing. But once again, no idea when that might be. And I think there’s lots of legal things that I don’t understand that need to be worked out in the meantime as well between my lawyers and their lawyers.
Have you ever had any acknowledgment on X itself from Elon Musk or anyone at xAI about this case? Has he ever spoken publicly about it?
No.
Would you expect him to?
I don’t think so. They clearly want to challenge this case, and so the best place to do that, I think, is in the courts and to leave it to see whether the merits of the case come through.
You were in New York recently to address the city council about your case. You didn’t get to speak to anyone directly at the company, is that right?
No. I mean, despite being subpoenaed, they didn’t turn up. Four of the other frontier AI companies did attend under subpoena. SpaceXAI didn’t, but they eventually did get their hearing with SpaceX in the city council. So, they have now had their opportunity to put questions and indeed did raise my case with them, I understand.
Was it a little enraging to attend a hearing like that where a company that you’re suing doesn't bother turning up?
I think it’s quite rude to the elected members of the New York City Council when you are a business that operates in New York. Indeed, I was told that they were just a few subway stops from City Hall. So I had traveled quite a long way from England to be there. And they couldn’t be bothered to turn up, which yeah, it felt arrogant and a bit of a snub, but they’ve now got there, so that’s a good thing.
Since you made the decision to take this to the courts, there have been a number of proposals in Parliament, notably there was a proposal for a kill switch bill at one point. Now I believe it’s dead or it’s not going very well. Is that right?
So, yes, there have been proposals put forward for a kill switch. And my understanding is the government rejected that. There continues to be strong calls for regulation of particularly superintelligent AI. We’ve heard various theories, whether it’s 2 percent, 10 percent, 20 percent risk of human extinction from this sort of race to superintelligence, a recursive AI, and we wouldn’t allow those margins of risk in any other sphere.
We would not allow it in bridge building or airplane making. They didn’t even allow it when they were testing the nuclear bomb and the Trinity test. It feels to me as though so much of this decision-taking is outside of democratic structures. It’s not with the public. It is being done by some incredibly, exceptionally wealthy companies and organizations who say they have the interests of the planet at heart.
But each time, actually, they’re asked about whether that is the future of humanity or whether they think that these risks could kill humanity, there’s a sort of shrugging of the shoulders and, “We’ll just keep going because we want to make money,” I guess.
It has been reported in the British press that there are members of Parliament, some of whom are working on committees to do with technology, who still don’t really understand what AI is. And clearly you’re not one of them because you’re aware of the dangers of this issue. But do you feel working across parties that you’re still having to explain technology and its dangers and possibilities to people who are making laws, or should be making laws, to protect the public from AI?
Well, look, I don’t think that’s only the case about AI. We are humans after all, and we have to deal with every single subject that exists under the sun. We have to get our heads around things that we’ve never heard of before.
A bit like being a journalist actually.
That’s true. But you have to then make laws and decisions. So, I don’t want to be unfair to my colleagues.
You may be a specialist in housing policy and you then need to get your head around AI. But I would say that this is the most important issue in front of anybody in parliament or politics at the moment, and therefore, everyone needs to get their head around AI.
My background is in social policy for women and children. But because we did quite a lot of work on the Online Safety Act when I was working for a children’s charity, we campaigned to get the age verification ban for children in pornography into the OSA. And indeed, created quite a strong piece of legislation in respect of that.
We had to get our heads around online safety on the online space. The problem was, of course, that act didn’t include AI chatbots. There were a number of amendments that tried to get it in and we would’ve been in a much better place had we actually succeeded.
But you know, I’m still not a tech expert even though I had quite a while to try to understand these things. But my view is that this is definitely the new front line of where harms are occurring. We can see that hugely in the increase in AI-generated child sexual abuse material, which is absolutely exploding.
In the end it comes down to the people who create the products. And that’s why we should be seeing digital product regulation in the same way as we would any other product regulation.
I’m very, very hopeful that the government is going to look at it really, really closely because there are always design choices that you can make and that can help to prevent these harms, these harms that are completely knowable. We can predict these harms, and so it should be easy to design them out from the start.
Companies can put in more safeguards. Why don’t they?
Profit. But also, let’s be honest, these are global tools and companies. So unless you have international agreement it is a bit like playing whack-a-mole, isn’t it?
The person who made that horrible video of me being chloroformed lives in the US, so the police aren’t gonna follow it up because they’re out of the country.
Do you know who did it?
I don’t know who they are, but the police did find who they were because it’s a criminal offense what they did. They just weren’t able to bring the charge.
We’ve spoken in the last 40 minutes about the full spectrum of human awfulness. I don’t think there’s any area of it that we haven’t …
Oh, sorry. Welcome to my life.
I’m really struck by how cheerful you are despite this. How do you remain so upbeat and hopeful while dealing with all of this?
Because you’ve always got to have hope for the future. I do have a really strong conviction that with the right group of people pushing toward a goal, you can achieve that. You don’t have to accept that things will always be like this. When people come together, when communities come together, you can act for change.
We’re just about to introduce our ban on strangulation in pornography, which is another thing that I’ve been campaigning for and introduced an amendment last year, which the government accepted.
There are always things that we can do to change. You just need to keep going. And also I would say that when you work with these terribly dark areas, yes, it can be quite vicariously traumatizing. But actually the people who work within the sectors are some of the most hopeful people, partly because if you lose hope, then it’s really bad. And we can’t because we’re talking about protecting vulnerable children, and we are fighting for women and our rights to be free of this harm.

Airlines seek more time to shift international flights to Navi Mumbai airport
MIAL presented its redevelopment plans and proposed temporarily shifting international traffic accounting for five million passengers per annum (MPPA) to NMIA.
Mumbai airport operator Mumbai International Airport Ltd (MIAL) has asked airlines to submit plans by November 3 for temporarily shifting international flights to Navi Mumbai International Airport (NMIA) ahead of the redevelopment of Terminal 1 (T1). Airlines have sought more time, people aware of the development said.
"At a meeting with the Airport Airline Operators Committee (AOC) on Wednesday, airlines indicated that the transition should not take place before the winter 2027 schedule, citing the need for advance planning," one person said.
"The airlines opposed any unilateral reduction in flight slots from the summer 2027 schedule and called on the airport operator to begin discussions on the winter schedule at the earliest, in line with the civil aviation ministry’s slot-allocation guidelines," they added.
The meeting lasted around 90 minutes and was attended by about 50 officials representing 35 airlines.
MIAL proposes shifting 5 million passengers to NMIA
During the meeting, MIAL presented its redevelopment plans and proposed temporarily shifting international traffic accounting for five million passengers per annum (MPPA) to NMIA.
IndiGo, the Air India group and Akasa Air have already finalised plans to shift international flights accounting for around 3 MPPA to the new airport. However, international airlines have yet to agree to the airport operator’s proposal.
MIAL has proposed shifting the remaining traffic from Terminal 2 (T2) at Mumbai airport during the summer 2027 schedule to meet its target, another person said.
The proposed relocation is part of MIAL’s plan to redevelop the ageing T1, which was commissioned in 1964.
Terminal 1 redevelopment to begin in April 2027
A spokesperson for Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (CSMIA) said structural audits conducted by Structwel in 2017 and IIT Bombay in 2024 highlighted safety and structural concerns. According to the airport operator, these findings make replacing the terminal necessary.
The spokesperson said the airport shared artistic impressions of the proposed terminal with the AOC on Wednesday. The images represent the intended design and passenger experience rather than a definitive preview of the final structure.
The redevelopment is expected to increase T1’s annual passenger-handling capacity from 15 MPPA to 20 MPPA. Demolition is scheduled to begin in April 2027, with completion targeted for December 2030.
To manage domestic traffic during the redevelopment, an expansion of the north-west pier of T2 is planned. The expanded section is expected to become operational by March 2029.
Mumbai airport capacity to rise to 65 MPPA
CSMIA currently handles around 55 million passengers annually. Its capacity is expected to increase to 65 MPPA after the redevelopment of T1 and the expansion of T2.
MIAL has said the temporary relocation of five million passengers would leave around 91% of the airport’s current traffic unaffected. The shifted international traffic is expected to return after the T2 expansion.
NMIA currently has a passenger-handling capacity of 20 MPPA and is eventually planned to handle 90 million passengers annually.

FCC clears Amazon Leo to acquire mobile-satellite operator Globalstar
The deal is designed to allow Leo to to deliver direct-to-device service.
Amazon Leo's $11.5 billion acquisition of mobile-satellite operator Globalstar has been approved by the US Federal Communications Commission (FCC), the regulator announced. The deal is designed to expand Leo's space-based footprint and allow direct-to-device service for its growing satellite network, Amazon previously said.
"The companies' complementary assets promise to enhance Amazon Leo's entry into the direct-to-device segment and create a stronger satellite operator capable of offering fixed and mobile services to residential, business, and government customers," the FCC wrote in a press release that echoed Amazon's own talking points. The regulator said that the deal is likely to benefit the public by enhancing data coverage in underserved areas.
You may not know Globalstar but have possibly used its services, as the company provides Apple's emergency satellite connectivity for compatible iPhones and Watches. Interestingly, Apple also held a 20 percent stake in Globalstar prior to its takeover. As part of the deal, Leo will power satellite services for supported iPhone and Apple Watch models.
Leo, a rival to SpaceX's Starlink, has been active of late. The company recently announced that it has 400 satellites in orbit and revealed last month that it had launched high-quality satellite internet service in Uzbekistan. It's teaming up with Delta to eventually bring satellite internet to flights, as well. Amazon recently added six new Arianespace launches and aims to have more than 3,000 low-earth orbit satellites up in the near future, still well short of SpaceX's 11,000 satellites.

As the U.S. midterm elections approached in late October, comments President Donald Trump made about peoples' bodies during his speeches at GOP campaign rallies gained widespread attention.
Trump's fixation on the physical attributes of the men and the women around him appeared to reflect his party's focus on gender roles and masculinity more broadly. "I examined his a** and then I looked at his shoulders," Trump said of Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio, on Oct. 17, eliciting a roar of applause. "I then patted him on the shoulder, and it was like a piece of steel. I'm still recovering."
By late October, another remark attributed to Trump, 80, circulated about rapper Nicki Minaj, who he told rallygoers had "one hell of a beautiful a**." The quote spread across multiple social media sites and prompted derisive comments from late-night talk show host Jimmy Kimmel.
The quote was correctly attributed to the president. Trump extolled the beauty of Minaj's body while stumping for Republican candidates in Michigan on Oct. 25. Videos of the event are widely available, including on C-SPAN (Trump's full comments beginning at 52:49).
"By the way, I looked at one hell of a beautiful a** before — Nicki Minaj," he said (at 0:20 below), pointing to a Gucci-clad Minaj in the audience, who covered her mouth and laughed. "That's hard to miss. That — stand up Nicki. That's hard to miss." The crowd laughed and whistled as she stood and waved.
Though Minaj has yet to openly address Trump's comments as of this writing, she did later join him on stage and pledged her allegiance to him, all the way through a theoretical third term (at 1:44:01). "I will continue to support you forever and ever," she said. "If you run again, I will support you again."
Minaj, an outspoken supporter of Trump and the GOP in recent years, emerged from Air Force One with the president on Oct. 25 and posted a video from inside the aircraft, where she sat down with White House spokesperson Steven Cheung to answer questions about Trump's role in the leadup to the midterms.
When asked about "these fake news polls," Minaj told Cheung: "We don't pay those polls any mind, obviously they are there to deter our voters from going out and casting their vote."
As of this writing, the majority of polls show voters favoring Democrats. The party out of power typically gains ground in midterm elections, according to New York Times polling researcher Caroline Soler.

US vice president JD Vance has opened a direct channel to one of Iran’s most powerful hard-liners in an attempt to revive peace negotiations according to a report by the Wall Street Journal. This developments comes even as US president Donald Trump threatens to resume military strikes in the coming weeks.
Vance sent a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council and a former commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), in an outreach intended to test whether Washington and Tehran can agree on a framework for negotiations. The letter was sent at Trump’s direction, according to one person familiar with the matter cited by WSJ, and the president is aware of the initiative.
Separately, Trump has denied directing Vance to initiate peace negotiations with Iran, saying the vice president’s contact concerned medical supplies. “Iran needs help with medical supplies. Basically, it’s getting supplies in to help people that are not well,” Trump told reporters at Joint Base Andrews when asked whether he had instructed Vance to begin peace talks.
The effort comes as Trump weighs a short, intense new attack on Iran after next week’s US midterm elections. 
Vance is seeking to establish whether diplomacy can avert another round of fighting, though the discussions have yet to produce a detailed peace proposal. Rezaei said last week that Iran would not negotiate with Washington until its core demands were met.
The outreach marks a delicate balancing act for Vance, who has publicly backed the war but privately expressed reservations about prolonging it. Before Trump launched “Operation Epic Fury” in February, Vance argued for more robust diplomacy. Trump later appointed him lead negotiator, and the vice president travelled abroad twice to meet Iranian counterparts in pursuit of an agreement to end the conflict.
A memorandum of understanding reached in June collapsed just two weeks after it was signed, amid competing interpretations of how shipping through the Strait of Hormuz would be restored. Subsequent negotiations, mediated by Qatar and Pakistan, have failed to break the deadlock. Washington wants Iran to make nuclear concessions upfront, while Tehran is demanding immediate economic relief.
Rezaei’s emergence as a key interlocutor could also reshape the diplomatic process, potentially sidelining figures such as Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi and parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf. A veteran of Iran’s 1980s war with Iraq who led the IRGC for years, Rezaei has become an influential voice as the threat of renewed US attacks grows.
Earlier this month, he warned that Iran could target the United Arab Emirates, as well as data centres and internet cables across the region. On Sunday, he met security chiefs from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey in Tehran in a rare engagement at that level, as regional powers sought to contain the conflict.
Trump, meanwhile, has alternated between pursuing a diplomatic settlement and threatening to bomb Iran into submission, with dismantling its nuclear programme a central national-security priority of his second term. He said last week that Washington was not negotiating with Tehran and suggested military action was imminent. During a campaign stop on Tuesday, he accused Iran of dragging out efforts to reach a deal and warned that waiting until after the election would not help it.
Republicans face the prospect of losing seats in the House and Senate in the midterms, with voters citing the war and rising fuel prices among their concerns. Vance, an early contender for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination, is therefore navigating a conflict that carries both foreign-policy and domestic political risks.
Trump has said the war will end only when he decides it should. Whether Vance’s backchannel can create a viable diplomatic path before the president orders another attack remains an open question.

Aga banned for fake prescription from family member
- Published
Ethiopian marathon runner Ruti Aga has been handed a six-year ban after she attempted to explain a positive test for a banned substance using a prescription from a non-existent clinic, issued by a doctor who turned out to be a family member.
Aga, who won the 2019 Tokyo Marathon, tested positive for methylprednisolone after winning a half marathon in China in March.
She received a two-year ban for testing positive for the prohibited steroid - used to reduce inflammation and classed as performance enhancing by the World Anti-Doping Agency (Wada).
The 32-year-old was given a further four-year ban for tampering with evidence and misleading investigators during an interview.
"Aga attributed her positive test to treatment for a knee injury, submitting a prescription from a clinic that did not exist, issued by a 'doctor' who turned out to be a family member with no medical registration with the relevant authority," the Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) said on Thursday.
"When questioned, the family member claimed to have used an old prescription pad from a former workplace. But that clinic confirmed the individual had never worked there and the prescription was not theirs."
Aga, who has finished second three times at World Marathon Majors, has been provisionally suspended since 10 September and the ban will run from that date.

China takes Mbappé apology 'seriously' after backlash over 'Chinese dictator' remark
China has acknowledged soccer star Kylian Mbappé's apology for comments seen as disrespectful to Mao Zedong, the founding leader of Communist China
BANGKOK -- China's Foreign Ministry said Wednesday it has taken soccer star Kylian Mbappé's apology “seriously” for comments considered to be disrespectful of Mao Zedong, the founding leader of Communist China, as the fallout over the issue continues.
Mbappé faced a backlash Tuesday over comments he made in an online interview, losing brand deals with at least three different Chinese companies. Beverage maker Dongpeng, dairy giant Mengniu and cheese maker Milkground said in similarly worded statements that they were ending agreements with the star forward, each saying they oppose “any words and actions that hurt national sentiment.”
“We take seriously the apology he has made,” said Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun in a daily press briefing Wednesday.
It remains to be seen whether Mbappé’s apology will help him regain the brand deals or other businesses he lost Tuesday. His team’s games remained unavailable to viewers in China Wednesday.
“Of course, once a public figure's speech and actions cross the limit, or step on a red line, … he becomes a brand's negative asset,” said the Communist Party's official mouthpiece, the People's Daily, in an online column Wednesday. “It is owing to principles and the necessity of business logic that Chinese platforms and companies take firm actions to cut off such a relationship.”
The incident is the latest in a string of cases in which China has leveraged its economic clout to compel foreign companies and individuals to apologize for perceived slights. In 2019, Chinese state television ceased broadcasting NBA games after then-Houston Rockets general manager Daryl Morey tweeted support for anti-government protesters in Hong Kong.
China Media Group also said that it has suspended broadcasts of matches in the Spanish league and other games featuring the French player and demanded an apology from La Liga, Mbappé and his club, Real Madrid.
Mbappé issued an apology Tuesday, saying, “My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world.”
“I apologize to everyone my words have upset,” Mbappé said in a statement. “This was absolutely not my intention. I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history, and I am sincerely sorry.”
On Tuesday, Spanish league president Javier Tebas quickly issued a public apology and stressed La Liga’s commitment to preserving its partnerships with China.
Real Madrid apologized later on Wednesday, joining Mbappé in expressing regret over the player’s remarks and reiterating its respect for the Chinese people.
CMG said it received the apology from Real Madrid, without adding further comment. Earlier, it demanded a formal apology, saying the club’s stance that a player was entitled to his personal opinion was unacceptable.
In a video clip, Mbappé is asked about his favorite meme of himself, and the soccer star replies that it was “a video someone made of a guy … I think he was a Chinese dictator” before the video shows an altered image depicting Mbappé's face on the blue-suited body of Mao Zedong.
Soccer fans online jokingly call the star — who's said to overshadow many of his teammates and even the teams he plays on — a dictator, and memes showing him as Mao or other autocratic leaders are widely circulated.
Mao Zedong was a revolutionary who led the Communist Party during its crucial early days, winning a civil war against the ruling Nationalist Party in China, and then founding the modern-day People’s Republic of China.
Mao is revered by many, even today. However, he left behind a complex legacy of authoritarian rule, having led campaigns, like the 1959-63 Great Leap Forward and the 1966-76 Cultural Revolution, which killed an estimated 31 million people through starvation and persecution.
But China's online censorship apparatus meant that even though news about Mbappé’s lost brand deals was trending Tuesday, not everyone knew what he said. Comments about top leaders are considered sensitive and his comment was not translated by the brands or state media who criticized his remarks.
“Maybe he said something he shouldn’t have again and hurt people’s feelings here in China,” said He Xiaodou on Wednesday. The Beijing finance worker said he heard about the controversy, but did not know what it was about exactly. “I just vaguely got the impression that it might have been something political.”
Others who did know took the comments in stride.
“I think maybe some people or some companies are overreacting on this issue,” said Li Zhi, a Beijing lawyer. “It's not a big deal. It's not the first time this happened.”

Reddit is adding a 'for you' feed for recommendations
The app will have a "following" tab to surface content from subreddits you've joined.
Reddit is changing up its main feed as it looks to emphasize more recommended content. The platform is splitting its feed into "for you," which will surface algorithmic recommendations, and "following" which shows posts from subreddits you've joined.
The change makes Reddit's central feed more like other mainstream social platforms. Up until now, the company has had one main feed that mixes in recommended posts alongside updates from subreddits you've joined. The new "for you" section will be more focused on allowing users to "discover relevant communities and conversations you might not otherwise come across," the company said in an update. With the change, Reddit will initially open to the new "for you" feed, but it will default to whichever feed you were last using the next time you launch the app.
The company is likely hoping the move will boost users' engagement with the platform. CEO Steve Huffman has said he wants to make it easier for casual users to come back to the service and that Reddit should find more ways to surface relevant posts, even if they are older. The company is also experimenting with video and audio versions of popular posts, some of which are from threads that are several years old.
So far, the company hasn't put those posts into a full-screen scrollable TikTok-like feed. But in its blog post announcing the change, Reddit said that it would "continue experimenting with ways people can more intentionally explore Reddit," including "new ways to navigate" the app. The company also said it's working on ways for users to offer feedback on recommended content to make it easier to fine tune its suggestions.

Cyclone Arnab hits India's Andhra Pradesh state as tens of thousands evacuate
Officials say Cyclone Arnab crossed India’s Andhra Pradesh coast early Wednesday, a day after tens of thousands of people were forced to evacuate from vulnerable coastal areas in the eastern state
HYDERABAD, India -- Cyclone Arnab crossed India 's Andhra Pradesh coast in the early hours of Wednesday, officials said, a day after tens of thousands of people were evacuated from vulnerable coastal areas in the eastern state.
Prakhar Jain, head of the state’s disaster management authority, said the cyclone had weakened slightly before landfall but brought heavy to very heavy rainfall to several coastal districts, triggering widespread disruption in affected areas.
State disaster management officials said late Wednesday morning that wind speeds were up to 135 kph (84 mph).
Officials said the cyclone was expected to weaken further as it moved inland, with wind speeds likely to ease later in the day.
There were no immediate reports of casualties, but some damage was observed.
The India Meteorological Department said the landfall process was complete and heavy rainfall as well as strong winds would continue under the cyclone's influence in coastal areas of Andhra Pradesh and parts of southern Odisha state.
Cyclone Arnab weakened to a "severe" cyclonic storm Wednesday, IMD said in an update.
According to officials at the state's disaster management authority, Cyclone Arnab’s outer bands began lashing parts of the Andhra Pradesh coast late Tuesday as the storm intensified over the Bay of Bengal and moved toward an earlier-than-expected landfall.
Authorities placed all the state's coastal districts on high alert Tuesday and began evacuating people from low-lying and flood-prone areas ahead of its landfall. They also canceled some train services as heavy rain and gusty winds had already started lashing parts of the coast, officials said. At least 89,000 people have so far been evacuated in Andhra Pradesh, according to an official statement.
The state’s disaster management authority said more than 12 million people live along the cyclone’s expected path.
Authorities set up over 2,000 cyclone shelters across 20 districts, while emergency alerts were being sent to the mobile phones of millions of residents, Jain said, according to the Press Trust of India news agency. More than 30,000 fishing boats were secured along the coast, while nearly 1,100 medical teams were deployed across affected areas to provide emergency assistance, he added.
In neighboring Odisha, officials planned to evacuate about 48,000 people from areas likely to be affected by the storm.

New RSS group registers with justice dept to lobby in America
RSS Friends’ Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) filing came just days before RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat held a major rally at Madison Square Garden in New York
A new organisation, RSS Friends registered with the US Department of Justice (DoJ) on August 27 as a foreign agent representing the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), despite the RSS’ previous assertions that it does not lobby in the US.
In its filings with the DoJ, RSS Friends explicitly listed the RSS as its “foreign principal” along with the address of the organisation’s new headquarters in Delhi’s Keshav Kunj. The newly registered group also disclosed that its work will remain primarily informational, but that it does not have a written employment or lobbying contract with the RSS with specified compensation and deliverables. RSS spokesperson Sunil Ambekar didn’t respond to queries seeking comment despite multiple reminders.
RSS Friends’ Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) filing came just days before RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat held a major rally at Madison Square Garden in New York. The RSS, celebrating its centenary this year, is the ideological fount of the Bharatiya Janata Party.
“RSS Friends’ proposed activities are primarily informational, educational, public-relations, and community-engagement activities. Consistent with its governing documents and applicable law, it may communicate with members of the public, journalists, media organisations, researchers, academic and policy institutions, community leaders, civil-society organisations, and, where appropriate, government agencies or officials,” the filing reads.
It added: “The absence of a written contract should not be understood as a representation that no relationship, request, understanding, coordination, authorisation, direction, or other relevant factual connection exists. RSS Friends will disclose the actual facts relevant to its activities.”
RSS Friends’ website provides more detail about its objectives, which tend to revolve around correcting “misconceptions about the RSS” pushed by “politically motivated actors” that have created “negative repercussions for the Indian diaspora, particularly Hindu Americans.” It is not clear how old the organisation is, but the rssfriends.org websie was first registered in 2017. It is also not clear when the current version of the website was launched.
Three individuals linked with RSS Friends are mentioned in the DoJ filings: Rajendra Sonarikar, Pratikkumar Suthar and Jayant Pant. Suthar’s Linkedin profile says he “coordinates global outreach in the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS)” and has served in his position since March 2024. Suthar is based in New Delhi while it is presently unclear where Sonarikar and Pant reside. RSS Friends did not respond to a request for comment from HT.
The new registration follows a prolonged controversy over the RSS’ lobbying in the United States. In November 2025, news outlet Prism reported that elite lobbying firm Squire Patton Boggs was hired to “introduce the RSS to US officials” through State Street Strategies, another lobbying outfit. Subsequent disclosures filed with the US DoJ showed that Squire Patton Boggs had been paid $330,000 for its work on behalf of the RSS in 2025. To be sure, the RSS categorically denied reports that it hired lobbyists in America. Squire Patton Boggs subsequently disclosed its contract was terminated on September 30, 2025.
The matter caused a significant political controversy in India in late 2025.
“This is hardly the first time that the RSS has betrayed national interest,” Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said in response to the matter at the time.
The registration of RSS Friends coincides with a systematic effort by the RSS to enhance its outreach to the United States. Prior to Mohan Bhagwat’s visit in August this year, the organisation’s second-in-command Dattatreya Hosabale undertook a multi-day tour of America in April. This was explained by Hosabale as an effort to interact with “influential opinion makers” in Western nations to communicate the RSS’ mission and objectives.

Cyclone Arnab makes landfall in Andhra Pradesh; trees uprooted, power supply disrupted
Gusty winds with speeds of 125-135 kmph have been reported in Kakinada, Konaseema and West Godavari districts and will continue over the next three hours
Severe cyclone Arnab made landfall on the Andhra Pradesh coast between Kakinada and Yanam of Puducherry early Wednesday affecting the entire coastal Andhra with destructive winds and torrential rains, disrupting normal life, authorities said.
According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the process of the extremely severe cyclone making landfall began on Tuesday night in Konaseema district and Narsapuram areas in West Godavari district.
A bulletin released by AP State Disaster Management Authority chairman Prakhar Jain at 6am on Wednesday said the landfall process of the very severe cyclone Arnab was continuing, with its “eye” located approximately 30km from Narsapur, 55km from Yanam, 70km from Kakinada and 90km from Machilipatnam.
“Gusty winds with speeds of 125-135 kmph have been reported in Kakinada, Konaseema and West Godavari districts and will continue over the next three hours,” Jain said.
According to reports being received in the control room at the state secretariat, uprooted trees, fallen electricity poles, damaged roads, inundated low-lying areas and widespread power outages were reported from Srikakulam in the north to Bapatla in the south.
Visakhapatnam district recorded the highest rainfall, with 200.20mm reported by midnight on Tuesday. Kothavalasa in Vizianagaram district received 162.75mm.
Sea waves in the Kakinada and Yanam regions reported to have risen to the heights of 1.5 to 2.5 metres, while reports from affected coastal stretches indicated waves surging much higher in some locations.
Road, rail transport hit
As many as 63 trains were cancelled and 15 others rescheduled in view of the deteriorating weather conditions. The Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (APSRTC) cancelled 160 services in Visakhapatnam district.
The government has imposed restrictions on night-time travel in Visakhapatnam and several other districts from Tuesday night as a precautionary measure.
Road connectivity was disrupted at multiple locations, including stretches of National Highway 16 between Kathipudi and Ongole, where traffic movement came to a standstill, according to reports from the affected areas.
Visakhapatnam affected by heavy rain and winds
Visakhapatnam bore the brunt of heavy rain and powerful winds, with seawater advancing significantly towards the city. Uprooted trees blocked roads and damaged vehicles. Electricity supply was disrupted across the city.
Extremely heavy rainfall was reported in Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram, Srikakulam, Parvathipuram Manyam, Anakapalli, Alluri Sitarama Raju, Kakinada and East Godavari districts.
The situation remained tense in coastal settlements as residents faced the combined threat of heavy rain, strong winds and rising sea levels.
Coastal damage reported in Kakinada and Konaseema
The coastal areas of Kakinada and Dr BR Ambedkar Konaseema districts were among the worst-affected regions as Cyclone Arnab intensified on Tuesday night.
What began as light rain in the morning developed into torrential downpours accompanied by powerful winds by nightfall, bringing normal life to a standstill. Waves surged along the coast, with reports from affected stretches indicating heights of five to eight metres.
At Kothapatnam near Uppada, a protective wall constructed with boulders was severely damaged by the force of the waves. Several motorcyclists travelling along coastal roads lost their balance amid the powerful winds and spray from the sea. Six people sustained minor injuries.
Uppada–Kakinada Beach Road damaged
Large stones placed as part of coastal erosion-control measures were broken apart or dislodged and scattered across the road, further obstructing movement.
Hundreds of electricity poles collapsed in Kakinada and Konaseema districts, while numerous hoardings were brought down by the winds. Several mobile towers were also tilted or damaged. With power supply to many towers interrupted, mobile communication signals failed in several areas.
At Allavaram, seawater reached the compound wall of an ONGC plant. Several tin-roofed sheds were blown away in villages, while poultry farms suffered extensive damage.
Yanam also witnessed the collapse of trees and electricity poles at several locations. A rehabilitation centre set up for evacuated residents was inundated, with water entering the entire ground floor. Officials shifted the occupants to the first floor to protect them from the rising water.
Residents moved to relief centres
Authorities had moved people from low-lying areas in several mandals of Kakinada and Konaseema districts to relief and rehabilitation centres as the cyclone’s impact intensified.

Around 3,000 people from Chinna Lanka, PM Lanka, East Thallu and Vemuladeevi villages were shifted to rehabilitation centres as a precaution against the cyclone and possible coastal inundation.
Coastal districts remain on high alert
With Cyclone Arnab’s landfall process expected to continue until the early hours of Wednesday, coastal districts remained on high alert. The combination of destructive winds, torrential rainfall, high waves and seawater intrusion had already caused extensive damage to transport infrastructure, electricity networks, roads, homes and agricultural fields.

France has released its Global Health Strategy for 2023-2027, in Lyon today, in the presence of three French Ministers, the Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs, the Minister of Health and Prevention, the Minister of Higher Education and Research, and WHO’s Director-General.
As a lead player for shaping global health policies, France has called on national and international stakeholders to support building a new global health architecture towards achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and in particular SDG3, focused on ensuring healthy lives and promoting well-being for all, at all ages.
The new Health Strategy aims to help reduce health inequalities and strengthen the One Health approach to better prevent and prepare for future global health emergencies. It urges the global community to address the health consequences of climate change and the environmental impact on health systems.
To underscore WHO’s and France strong collaboration and in recognition of France’s pivotal global health role, Dr Tedros travelled to France to join the launch event.
“France was a founding member of WHO in 1948 and has been a strong friend to WHO throughout the 75 years since then,” said Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General. “As one of the world’s largest economies, France has a critical role to play in global health, and the new Global Health Strategy will enhance that role. It aligns well with WHO’s priorities to promote, provide, protect, empower and perform for health.”
France shares key health priorities with WHO, adopting a crosscutting approach and prioritizing universal health coverage (UHC) as part of the 2030 Sustainable Development Agenda. France also provides support for transformative initiatives at WHO such as the WHO Academy and the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) which the Ministers visited today.
Dr Tedros addressed the audiences at the Academy and IARC together with Ms Catherine Colonna, Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs, Mr Aurélien Rousseau, Minister of Health and Prevention, and Ms Sylvie Retailleau, Minister of Higher Education and Research.
"The World Health Organization, whose 74th anniversary we are celebrating today, must continue to play a central and driving role,” said Ms Catherine Colonna, the French Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs. “France will continue to support the WHO and its ambitious governance and financing reforms."
"France is also committed alongside the WHO Academy through several partnership with universities, research institutes, and public health institutions," remarked Sylvie Retailleau, Minister of Higher Education and Research. "Our goal is to enrich the learners' experience through a diversified training portfolio within the Academy."
"The launch of this Global Health Strategy is the perfect opportunity to celebrate the 75th anniversary of the WHO. The Organization plays a central role in global health, and we must continue to support it," said Mr Aurélien Rousseau, Minister of Health and Prevention. "This is why, I am announcing today, France is keen to host, in the first quarter of 2024, in partnership with the WHO, the first international financing conference for the fight against meningitis."
The 2023-2027 French Strategy for Global Health is the fruit of collaboration involving a wide range of French actors: public agencies, civil society organizations, higher education and research organizations, scientific institutions, foundations, organizations of human, animal and environmental health specialists, local government bodies and the private sector. They will all be represented within a monitoring committee to track the Strategy’s implementation and progress.

The Indian Institute of Technology Bombay on Friday said its researchers have developed a low-cost device that can screen for anaemia and sickle cell disease using a drop of blood.
A research team from the Department of Chemical Engineering, led by Mahesh Tirumkudulu, has developed a simple, low-cost point-of-care approach that uses the length of a blood smear (the distance that a drop of blood spreads across a glass slide) to detect anaemia, and detect and monitor treatment for sickle cell disease. IIT Bombay said.
Prof Tirumkudulu's team built their own automated device to have a uniform method of creating a smear. Under these controlled conditions, the researchers observed that blood from different people gives different smear lengths, and this difference holds useful information.
Prof. Tirumkudulu explained that more viscous blood spreads less easily and, therefore, produces a shorter and thicker smear under the same conditions.
Once the team confirmed that the method could sense small differences in blood viscosity, they decided to investigate whether those differences could help identify disease. It was found that anaemia lowers red blood cell concentration and haemoglobin, while sickle cell disease makes red blood cells rigid.
The researchers said their patented automated smearing device can be manufactured cost-effectively. Also, the test itself requires only a pipette, glass slides, an inexpensive chemical, vials for the sickling treatment, and a ruler or imaging device to measure smear length, they added.
"This makes our technique particularly useful in places where conventional diagnostic laboratories are difficult to access, and it doesn't require any special expertise to use," said Dr. Mahrukh Mir, a former PhD scholar in Prof Tirumkudulu's lab, and the first author of the study.
The researchers pointed out that blood viscosity cutoffs vary for various groups of people because certain genetic differences affect how blood reacts when oxygen levels drop.
Also, the anaemia test could miss identifying some patients when the usual link between viscosity and anaemia does not hold, such as in a rare condition called hyperviscosity syndrome, where blood plasma is unusually thick.
Currently, the technology is licensed to Rheoheme Private Limited, an IIT Bombay startup, and the team is now working with the National Institute for Research in Tribal Health, Jabalpur, in Madhya Pradesh and All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) Nagpur, toward regulatory approval, while exploring extending the device to measure clotting time and glucose levels.
"Our initial aim was to understand the physics of spreading blood drop, and that led to the medical applications," added Prof Tirumkudulu.

I've been singing the praises of merino wool in these pages for over five years. Most people have come around to the fact that merino wool is a super fiber; it's both sustainable and quite remarkable in its capabilities. Merino wool somehow manages to be comfortable in 95-degree heat, and it'll insulate you against below-freezing temperatures. Unlike synthetic fibers derived from petroleum, merino wool resists odors and is naturally breathable. What's not to love? The price.
Merino wool isn't cheap. That's why I love these merino T-shirts from Quince: They're just $42.
The Quince All-Season T-shirt is 100 percent extra-fine merino wool with a 165-gsm weave, which is perfect even on the warmest summer days where I live. (Admittedly, I think the hottest it got this summer was 92 Fahrenheit). I like the relaxed fit here as well. It's neither skintight technical nor overly loose and baggy. It fits like a T-shirt is supposed to. That's what Quince does well in a number of categories: offer a solid, no-nonsense, competitively priced merino wool T-shirt that fits well and feels great. As an added bonus, Quince offers free shipping and free returns for 365 days. I haven't actually tested either—I haven't needed to, my Quince T-shirt is still going strong after two years of use. But there are plenty of customer reviews on Reddit suggesting the company does honor that offer.
Not sold on the idea of a wool T-shirt? I understand. When I started testing merino, I too had visions of lumberjacks in plaid and itchy sweaters someone's grandma had knitted. None of that is merino wool. Merino sheep have thinner, softer wool, which has evolved to keep them comfortable across a wide range of temperatures and is comfortable to wear next to your skin.
One wool myth that's not just a myth is care. Merino isn't cotton. Quince's care instructions for the All Season T-shirt say to wash it in cold water and lay flat to dry. The latter is important, as hanging merino wool to dry will stretch it out (because of the water weight). Can you throw it in the dryer? Yes. I have, for testing purposes only. It will shrink, and it will wear it out much, much faster, but you can do it.
